audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree about three of the seven stages. content.win reads Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Zac while full.phases sides read Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Skill/Fiora/Skill/Fiora. Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items each carry a different verdict depending on which layer the page renders.
audit.why: The 2+ items disagreement is the worst of the three: full.phases[6].side said Fiora while its own why text reads "your side-lane pattern is at full power", and the content layer's whys[6] and late both say the matchup flips to Zac. The stage label contradicted its own body text.
audit.corrected: Aligned both layers to Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Fiora/Skill/Zac — full.phases[3].side to Fiora, full.phases[6].side to Zac, content.win[5] to Skill.

audit.why: The flagged "level chart contradicts data" defect is only partly a data error. Zac wins 54.55% over 154 games while genuinely losing the lane — he is a teamfight engage tank against a duelist, so his win rate is earned after laning, not during it. I reconciled the two layers and moved First item to Skill, but I did not invent Zac lane stages to make the chart match the win rate.

The content layer already handles the decisive interaction correctly: Riposte parries and stuns a Zac engage, and wants.you[0] plus spikes[0] both tell the player to bait W before committing E or Q. This is the single most important thing in the matchup and it was already right — no correction needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns said "Bait it. Track it before every engage" without ever giving Riposte's cooldown, so the player has no idea how long the window after a baited W actually is.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s. Fiora maxes Q or E first, so through most of lane W sits at rank 1 on a 24s cooldown — longer than Zac's own Elastic Slingshot at 21s. A baited Riposte is one of the largest punish windows in the top lane and the entry never quantified it.
audit.corrected: Stated Riposte 24s at rank 1 / 16s maxed against Zac E at 21s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Zac's health stacking is itself a liability into Fiora.
audit.why: Lunge applies on-hit effects, so Fiora scales cleanly into percent-max-health on-hit itemisation. Zac's core build is Heartsteel, which makes every point of health he stacks worth more to her. The entry recommended armour as though this were a normal physical-damage duel.
audit.corrected: Noted that Lunge applies on-hit and that stacking health feeds it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] pairs the title "Build armor" with the body "Fiora wastes Riposte — commit the full pattern immediately", and full.phases[1].why refers to Fiora as "he".
audit.why: Same generator template mismatch seen in the Darius entry — the Do title and its explanation describe different things. The armour advice also needs a caveat, since Grand Challenge deals percent true damage that armour does not touch.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the body at the armour title with the true-damage caveat, and fixed the pronoun.

edits.before: First item still favours Fiora's clean duel over your early tank stats.
edits.after: First item is a coin-flip — her clean duel against your tank bulk.

edits.before: With her first item Fiora out-duels you cleanly — she kites your slow abilities, procs vitals, and Riposte negates your engage window whenever it's up.
edits.after: Her first item out-duels you cleanly, and Lunge applies on-hit — percent-HP on-hit scales off the health you stack, so armour alone reads the trade wrong.

edits.before: Q-stretch trades and blob pickups out-sustain the early chip. Identify how Fiora contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Lunge pokes you for free and Riposte threatens any answer, so soak XP at range and never spend E while her W is available.

edits.before: Every blob you collect is a trade he paid for. Only take the trade when Fiora's Riposte is down.
edits.after: Every blob you collect is a trade she paid for. Only take the trade when Fiora's Riposte is down.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Fiora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grand Challenge reveals all four vitals and heals her on completion; against your health pool those are cheap true-damage hits.

edits.before: - Fiora Riposte: matchup-defining — Parries + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Fiora Riposte: 24s at rank 1, 16s maxed — it parries all damage and stuns you if it catches your knockup. Bait it and you own the next 20s. - Your Elastic Slingshot: 21s at rank 1, never spent on chip.

edits.before: Fiora wastes Riposte — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Armour blunts Lunge and Bladework, but her R vitals are true.

notes: The "level chart contradicts data" defect is only half a data error here, and I did not fully flatten it. Zac wins 54.55% over 154 games while genuinely losing the 1v1 to Fiora at every lane stage — the win rate is earned by grouping and engaging, not by winning the sidelane. I reconciled the two layers against each other (they disagreed on three of seven stages, including 2+ items where the full layer's side label contradicted its own body text) and moved First item to Skill, but I refused to invent Zac lane stages purely to make the chart track the win rate; a player who trusted that would take a duel that kills them. DATA BUG worth fixing at the source: champ-data/_kits/zac.json carries a "grounding" flag on Elastic Slingshot. Zac's E does not ground anyone — the flag is a text-match false positive off the description "Zac attaches his arms to the ground". It has already propagated into _missing-interactions.json, which now asserts "Zac can deny your mobility (Lunge (Q)) with Elastic Slingshot (E)" for the Fiora file and the same claim in the Galio file. Any entry generated from that rule will tell players Zac can deny dashes, which is false. I wrote nothing based on it.
